> In the western sky appears the **Padmaketu** <note>The "Lotus Comet"</note>.
> It is as white as a lotus stalk and remains visible for only a single night.
> It brings seven years of great abundance and extreme joy to the people. ॥ 49 ॥

> The comet known as **Avarta** <note>The "Circular" or "Whirling" comet</note> appears at midnight in the west.
> Its crest points to the left, it is glossy, and it possesses the reddish hue of the dawn.
> For as many moments as it remains visible, for that many months will it ensure prosperity. ॥ 50 ॥

> Appearing in the west during the twilight is the comet named **Samvarta** <note>The "Destroyer" or "World-Ender"</note>.
> It has a smoke-colored and copper-hued crest; it is a fierce omen that covers one-third of the sky.
> It stands terrifyingly, like the point of a trident <note>original: "śūlāgra"</note>. ॥ 51 ॥

> For as many hours <note>term: "muhūrta"; a unit of time approximately 48 minutes long</note> as it is visible, for that many years does it destroy the world.
> It kills kings through the clash of weapons and brings suffering to the region of its rising constellation. ॥ 52 ॥

> Aside from those comets previously described as auspicious, when a constellation <note>term: "nakṣatra"; one of the 27 lunar mansions of Hindu astrology</note> is clouded by smoke or touched by a comet,
> The kings of the following nations will face destruction, as I shall now declare. ॥ 53 ॥

# The Great Compilation
## Chapter 11

If a comet appears in the constellation of **Ashwini**, it destroys the ruler of the **Ashmaka** <note>A region in ancient central India, likely near the Godavari river</note> people.
If in **Bharani**, it shall slay the king of the **Kiratas** <note>A generic term for mountain-dwelling tribes or foresters</note>.
In **Krittika** <note>referred to here as Bahula</note>, it destroys the Lord of **Kalinga** <note>Modern-day Odisha</note>.
In **Rohini**, it destroys the king of the **Surasenas** <note>The region around Mathura</note>.

In **Mrigashirsha** <note>referred to as Saumya</note>, it destroys the ruler of **Ushinara**.
Likewise, in **Ardra**, it destroys the masters of those who live by the products of the water <note>fishermen or aquatic traders</note>.
In **Punarvasu** <note>referred to as Aditya</note>, it destroys the Lord of **Ashmaka**.
In **Pushya**, it destroys the sovereign of **Magadha** <note>The powerful ancient kingdom in modern Bihar</note>.

In **Ashlesha** <note>referred to as Bhujanga</note>, it destroys the king of the **Asikas**.
In **Magha** <note>referred to as Pitrya</note>, it destroys the king of **Anga**.
In **Purva Phalguni** <note>referred to as Bhagya</note>, it destroys the Lord of the **Pandyas** <note>The southern dynasty of the Tamil region</note>.
In **Uttara Phalguni** <note>referred to as Aryamna</note>, it destroys the ruler of **Ujjain**.
In **Hasta** <note>referred to as Savitra</note>, it destroys the king of the **Dandakas**.

In **Chitra**, the expert should predict the death of the ruler of **Kurukshetra**.
In **Svati** <note>referred to as Prabhanjana</note>, the kings of **Kashmir** and **Kamboja** <note>An ancient region in the far northwest, near modern Afghanistan/Tajikistan</note> shall cease to exist.

If it should be in **Vishakha**, the kings of the **Ikshvakus** and **Alaka** <note>referred to as Ratnanatha</note> are slain.
In **Anuradha** <note>referred to as Maitra</note>, the sovereign of **Pundra** <note>Part of ancient Bengal</note> is affected.
In **Jyeshtha**, there is the death of the **Universal Emperor** <term>Sarvabhauma: a ruler whose chariot rolls everywhere without obstruction</term>.

In **Mula**, the kings of the **Westerners** and **Madra** perish.
In **Purva Ashadha** <note>referred to as Jaladeva</note>, death comes to the King of **Kashi** <note>Modern Varanasi</note>.

# The Great Compilation
## Chapter 12: The Rising of Agastya

->**The Deeds of the Sage**<-

The ocean was made exceedingly beautiful by that Sage <note>The Sage Agastya, associated with the star Canopus</note> when he suddenly caused the depletion of its waters. The sea then revealed its inner mountains, whose peaks had been torn asunder by the claws of sea monsters. With its falling sprays of water mixed with pearls and the finest gems, the ocean seemed to mock the gods by displaying its own white crowns of jewels from ages past. **(1)**

Even when its waters were taken away, the ocean shone even more brilliantly. It was adorned by mountains of coral and the lightning-like flashes of precious gems, as well as the serpents emerging from their depths. **(2)**

The great ocean, though reduced to a state of distress <note>literally "fallen into calamity" by being drained</note>, was made to possess the splendor of the gods by him. Even with its water reduced to the amount contained in a small boat, it remained filled with shimmering whales, water-elephants, and serpents, while heaps of jewels were cast about its floor. **(3)**

Though its water was stolen, the Lord of Rivers <note>The Ocean</note>—strewn with shells produced from the digestion of moving whales—retained the beauty of a lake in autumn. It appeared as if filled with white lotuses and swans, represented by the foam of its remaining waves. **(4)**

He <note>Agastya</note> transformed the ocean into a likeness of the autumn sky: the whales were the dark clouds, the gems were the stars, the pure crystal was the moon, and the rays from the jewels on the hoods of serpents were the fiery planets. The sky itself seemed to have bent down to the earth. **(5)**

Whose moving peaks once rose up to block the path of the Sun's chariot, and upon whose slopes the startled celestial musicians <term>Vidyadharas</term> clung to their beloveds, who in their agitation offered their bodies in embrace—

# The Great Compilation

The pond, with its circling waves, seems to open its beautiful-lashed eyes—the white water-lilies with bees nestled in their petals—to gaze upon the splendor of the moon, now freed from the veil of the monsoon clouds <note>original: "payoda-vigama"</note>, like a face with dark pupils. || 10 ||

With her hands—the lakes filled with various colorful lotuses, swans, ruddy geese, and ducks—and bearing abundant gems, flowers, and fruits, the Earth herself seems to offer a respectful greeting <note>term: "arghya" (a traditional offering to an honored guest)</note> to the one named Agastya. || 11 ||

The waters that were fouled by the poisonous fire of serpents—those creatures whose bodies are coiled within the thick mud of the mountain beds—become pure and auspicious once more at the mere sight of the star Agastya. || 12 ||

If the mere memory of this "Son of Varuna" <note>original: "Varunankaruha," a mythological epithet for the sage Agastya</note> washes away sins, how much more so his praises? I shall now describe the ritual of offering <note>original: "ardha-vidhi," likely a scribal variant for "argha-vidhi"</note> as declared by the ancient seers, for the benefit of kings. || 13 ||

A wise man should announce the appearance of the star after calculating its visibility for each specific region. In the city of Ujjain, this occurs when the true Sun has reached seven degrees <note>original: "svara-khyaih," where 'svara' (musical notes) numerically represents the number seven</note> of the sign of Virgo. || 14 ||

When the darkness of night is slightly pierced by the nether-rays of the dawn in the southern direction...

# The Great Compilation <note>original: "Brihat Samhita"</note> | [Chapter 12]

Once the directions have been properly identified by the Royal Astrologer <note>term: Samvatsara (an astronomer-priest skilled in time-keeping)</note>, the King, remaining pure and restrained, should offer the respectful libation <note>term: Arghya (a ritual offering of water and auspicious items)</note> upon the earth. || 15 ||

This should be performed with fragrant seasonal flowers and fruits, with gems born of the ocean, and with gold and fine garments; with a cow and a bull, and with edible offerings mixed with sweetened rice-milk <note>original: "paramanna"</note>; with curd, unbroken grains, fragrant incense, and ointments. || 16 ||

The King who presents this offering with faith, being freed from the faults of disease and having conquered the host of his enemies, shall prosper. If he performs this correctly for seven years, he attains sovereignty over the entire earth, whose girdle is the ocean. || 17 ||

The twice-born <note>term: Dvija (members of the upper three social classes, here likely referring to Brahmins)</note> who offers this libation according to his means obtains the knowledge of the Vedas, women, and sons. The merchant <note>term: Vaishya</note> gains cattle and abundant wealth, the laborer <note>term: Shudra</note> gains the destruction of disease, and all obtain the fruits of righteousness. || 18 ||

If the star named Agastya <note>note: The star Canopus, whose rising signaled the clearing of waters in ancient India</note> appears harsh, it causes disease; if tawny, a lack of rain; if smoky, it brings misfortune to cattle; and if it flickers, it leads to fear. If it resembles the color of madder <note>note: a reddish dye</note>, it causes hunger and war; and if it appears minute, it brings the siege of cities. || 19 ||

But if it appears like gold <note>original: "shatakumbha"</note> or with the luster of crystal, as if saturating the earth with its flood of rays, then the earth becomes rich with abundant food and populated by people free from fear and disease. || 20 ||

->Under **Pushya** <note>The 'Nourishing' constellation</note> are barley, wheat, rice, sugarcane, forests, ministers, and kings;<-
->those who live by water, holy men, and those dedicated to performing sacrifices and rituals.<-

# The Great Compilation
## Chapter 15

Under the star **Magha** <note>original: "Pitri"; the star associated with the Ancestors</note>, one finds those wealthy in wealth and grain, granaries, mountain-dwellers, those devoted to their ancestors, merchants, heroes, eaters of raw flesh <note>likely referring to predatory animals or certain forest tribes</note>, and men who harbor a dislike for women.

In the **Purva-Phalguni** <note>The "Former Reddish One"</note> star are actors, young women, the amiable, musicians, artisans, commodities, cotton, salt, honey, oil, and young boys.

Under **Uttara-Phalguni** <note>original: "Aryaman"; the star associated with the solar deity of patronage</note> are those devoted to mildness, purity, modesty, heretical sects, charity, and the study of sacred texts; also fine grains, the immensely wealthy, those devoted to righteousness, and kings.

In the star **Hasta** <note>The "Hand"</note> are thieves, elephants, chariot-drivers, high officials, artisans, commodities, husked grains, those endowed with Vedic knowledge, merchants, and the energetic.

Under **Chitra** <note>original: "Tvashtra"; the star associated with the divine architect</note> are those skilled in jewelry, gems, dyeing, painting, music, and perfumery; also clever mathematicians, weavers, ophthalmic surgeons <term>Shalakya: practitioners of the branch of medicine dealing with the eyes, ears, nose, and throat</term>, and royal grains.

In **Swati** <note>The "Independent One"</note> are birds, wild animals, horses, merchants, grains, and things characterized by an abundance of wind <note>referring to the "Vata" element or airy temperaments</note>.

->**The Influence of the Constellations**<-

Under the constellation of **Vishveshvara** <note>original: "विश्वेश्वर" (Viśveśvara); another name for the Nakshatra Uttarāṣāḍhā, ruled by the "Universal Gods"</note> are those who serve as high-ranking royal officials <term>Mahamatra: a high minister or chief executive</term>, professional wrestlers, and those devoted to the care of elephants, horses, and the gods. Also included are those who deal in immovable property, warriors, those who lead a life of enjoyment, and men endowed with great physical vigor. **|| 19 ||**

In **Shravana** <note>The "Ear" constellation</note> are those skilled in illusions or magic, those who are perpetually active and capable in their duties, the energetic, the righteous, the devotees of Vishnu <term>Bhagavatas: followers of the devotional path of Vaishnavism</term>, and those who speak the truth. **|| 20 ||**

In the constellation of **Vasubha** <note>original: "वसुभ" (Vasubha); another name for Dhanishta, ruled by the eight Vasus or elemental deities</note> are men free from pride, the impotent, those whose friendships are fickle, and those disliked by women. Also found here are those devoted to charity, those possessed of great wealth, and those who are naturally peaceful. **|| 21 ||**

Under the domain of **Varunesha** <note>original: "वरुणेश" (Varuṇeśa); the constellation Shatabhisha, ruled by Varuna, god of the cosmic waters</note> are those who use nets <note>such as trappers</note>, fishermen, those who deal in aquatic products, and those who earn a living from water-dwelling creatures. This group also includes hog-butchers, washermen, distillers of liquor, and bird-catchers. **|| 22 ||**

In **Aja** <note>original: "आज" (Āja); the constellation Purva Bhadrapada, ruled by Aja Ekapada</note> are thieves, shepherds, the violent, plowmen, and those of low or dishonest conduct. Also included are men devoid of religious vows or righteousness, and those skilled in hand-to-hand combat. **|| 23 ||**

In **Ahirbudhnya** <note>original: "अहिर्बुध्न्य" (Ahirbudhnya); the constellation Uttara Bhadrapada, ruled by the "Serpent of the Deep"</note> are the Brahmins <note>the priestly and scholarly class</note>, those engaged in sacrifices, charity, and penance, and those of great wealth.

# The Great Compilation ## [Chapter 15]

->Hermits, religious hypocrites <note>original: "pāṣaṇḍā"; refers to those who take up false or non-Vedic asceticism</note>,<-

In the mansion of **Revati** <note>original: "pauṣṇe"; dedicated to the deity Pushan</note> are those products born of water, fruits, flowers, salt, gems, conch shells, pearls, and lotus seeds; fragrant flowers, perfumes, merchants, and ship-captains. [25]

In **Bharani** <note>original: "yāmye"; dedicated to Yama, the god of death</note> are those who feed on blood and flesh, the cruel, those engaged in killing, binding, and beating; husk-grains <note>such as chaff-covered cereals</note>, those of low birth, and those devoid of courage. [27]

The three "Prior" mansions <note>Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, and Purva Bhadrapada</note> along with **Krittika** <note>the fire-deity's star</note> belong to the Brahmins <note>the priestly class</note>. The three "Latter" mansions <note>Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, and Uttara Bhadrapada</note> along with **Pushya** belong to the Kings. The mansions of **Revati**, **Anuradha**, **Magha**, and **Rohini** <note>the star of the Creator, Prajapati</note> belong to the tillers of the soil. [28]

**Punarvasu**, **Hasta**, **Abhijit**, and **Ashvini** are declared the stars of the merchant folk. **Mula**, **Chitra**, **Svati**, and **Shatabhisha** are the stars for those of fierce nature <note>original: "ugrajāteḥ"</note> in their exercise of power. [29]

# The Great Compilation
## [ Chapter 16 ]

> The lunar mansions presided over by the deities Soma <note>Mrigashira</note>, Indra <note>Jyeshtha</note>, Chitra, and the Vasus <note>Dhanishta</note> are said to govern those in service and those who hold lordship. The mansions of the Serpents <note>Ashlesha</note>, Vishakha, Shravana, and Bharani are designated as belonging to the class of the Chandalas <note>term: Chandala; historically refers to marginalized groups or those outside the traditional social order</note>. || 30 ||

> A lunar mansion is said to be "afflicted" when it is occupied by the Sun or Saturn, or when it is marred by a stationary period, a retrograde motion, or a "piercing" <note>a specific astronomical conjunction</note> by Mars. It is likewise afflicted when involved in an eclipse, struck by a meteor, or clearly distressed by the Moon. || 31 ||

> Such a mansion is called "struck," as is one that undergoes an unnatural change in appearance. The destruction of the social classes previously mentioned is predicted through these afflictions; conversely, if the opposite conditions occur, it leads to prosperity. || 32 ||

-> Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, titled "The Array of the Lunar Mansions," <-
-> in the *Great Compilation* composed by Sri Varahamihira. <-

> The Mekalas, the Kiratas, the Vitakas, those born within and outside the mountains, and the Pulindas.

The disgraces of their families, the violent, the ungrateful, thieves, and those devoid of truth, purity, and charity. Those who travel on donkeys, those skilled in wrestling, the intensely angry, the cruel-hearted, and the low-born.

Afflicted people, the deceitful, the demonic, and all creatures who sleep excessively. Those who have abandoned righteousness, as well as crops of black gram and sesame; all these are governed by the Sun and the Moon <note>original: "arka-shashinoh"</note>.

Those living in mountain fortresses, the Pallavas, the White Huns <note>original: "shveta-huna"</note>, the Cholas, the Afghans <note>original: "avagana"</note>, the Marus, and the Chinese. Those living on the frontiers, the wealthy, the ambitious, and those endowed with perseverance and valor.

Those who take pleasure in the wives of others and in disputes, those curious about the weaknesses of others, the intoxicated, the foolish, the unrighteous, and those desiring victory; all these are declared to be under the dominion of the Comet <term>Ketu: the descending lunar node, often depicted as a comet or a headless celestial body</term>.

If the planet <note>referring to the ruling body of a specific group</note> is large, possesses glossy rays, and remains in its natural state at the time of its rising; if it is not afflicted by portents such as thunderbolts, meteors, dust storms, or planetary conjunctions; and if it occupies its own zodiacal house or its sign of exaltation while being aspected by beneficial planets, it brings prosperity to those over whom it is said to preside.

# The Great Compilation

## The Great Compilation

According to the ancient sages such as Parāśara <note>Parāśara is a revered Vedic seer and the father of Vyāsa; he is considered one of the foundational authorities on Indian astrology</note> and others, a "planetary war" <note>original: "yuddha"; a phenomenon where two planets appear very close in the sky</note> is of four types, determined by their approach, contact, or positioning: Cleaving, Grazing, Clashing of Rays, and Passing to the Left. || 3 ||

In the case of **Cleaving**, there is a destruction of rain and a rift between friends and noble families. In **Grazing**, there is danger from weapons, conflict among ministers, and a scarcity of beloved foodstuffs. || 4 ||

In the **Clashing of Rays**, there are wars among kings, injuries from weapons, and suffering from hunger. In a war where a planet **Passes to the Left**, there likewise occur battles between monarchs. || 5 ||

The Sun is known as the *Crier* <note>original: "Ākranda"; representing the king or the force that comes to the rescue</note> when in the center; a planet in the East is the *City-Dweller* <note>original: "Paura"; representing the established citizens or the capital</note>, and one in the West is the *Marcher* <note>original: "Yāyī"; representing an invading force or expeditionary army</note>. Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn are always *City-Dwellers*, while the Moon is always the *Crier*. || 6 ||

The Comet <note>Ketu</note>, Mars, Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, and Venus are the *Marchers*. If these planets are defeated in the celestial war, they destroy their respective earthly counterparts—the Criers, Marchers, or City-Dwellers. If they are victorious, they grant victory to their own class. || 7 ||

When a *City-Dweller* planet is defeated by another *City-Dweller*, the citizens will destroy their own city's rulers.

# The Brihat Samhita

### Chapter 17: On the Warfare of the Planets

Thus are the "Attacker" and the "Appealer" defined,
As well as the "City-dweller" and the "Traveler" planets. <note>These are technical classifications of planets based on their positions and motions during a conjunction.</note> || 8 ||

A planet is considered defeated if it is situated to the south, appears harsh or dim, is trembling, retreats before reaching its destination, is minute in size, is "mounted" <note>overtaken by another</note>, appears unnatural, is devoid of brilliance, or is discolored. || 9 ||

A planet is declared victorious if it possesses characteristics opposite to those mentioned above. Even if situated to the south, a planet is victorious if it is large, glossy, and radiant. || 10 ||

If both planets in a conjunction are radiant, large, and glossy, it signifies mutual affection between them. If they are both the opposite <note>dim and small</note>, they bring destruction to their own sides. || 11 ||

If the characteristics of a "war" or a "conjunction" are indistinct or unclear, then the results for the kings on Earth will likewise be indistinct and difficult to determine. || 12 ||

When Mars <note>original: "Avanisuta" - son of the Earth</note> is defeated by Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note>, the people of Bactria <note>original: "Bahlika"</note>, those who are traveling, and those who are prosperous suffer. When Mars is defeated by Mercury <note>original: "Shashija" - son of the Moon</note>, the people of Shurasena, Kalinga, and Salva are oppressed. || 13 ||

# The Great Compilation (Brihat Samhita) | [Chapter 17]

When Saturn <note>original: "Saura"</note> is defeated by Mars <note>original: "Ara"</note>, the citizens of the capital cities emerge victorious, but the common subjects suffer. However, if Venus <note>original: "Shukra"</note> is the victor over Saturn, then granaries, storehouses, and the <term>Mlecchas</term> <note>a term used for non-Vedic or foreign peoples</note> are destroyed and afflicted by great distress. || 14 ||

When Mercury <note>original: "Shashija," literally 'son of the Moon'</note> is defeated by Mars <note>original: "Bhauma"</note>, then trees, rivers, ascetics, the people of the Ashmaka region, and great kings suffer. Furthermore, those residing in the northern direction and those initiated for <term>Yajnas</term> <note>sacrificial rituals</note> undergo great torment. || 15 ||

When Mercury is defeated by Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note>, then the <term>Mlecchas</term>, the laboring class <note>original: "Shudra"</note>, thieves, wealthy citizens, the people of Trigarta <note>modern-day Kangra region</note>, and those living in the mountains are oppressed, and the very earth trembles. || 16 ||

When Mercury is destroyed by Saturn <note>original: "Ravija," literally 'son of the Sun'</note>, then sailors, warriors, the ignorant, the wealthy, and pregnant women are all endangered. If Mercury is defeated by Venus <note>original: "Bhrigu"</note>, there is a danger of fire, and the destruction of crops, clouds, and those who are traveling. || 17 ||

When Venus is struck by Jupiter, the peoples of Kuluta, Gandhara <note>ancient region in modern-day Pakistan/Afghanistan</note>, Kaikeya, Madra, Salva, Vatsa, and Vanga <note>ancient Bengal</note> perish, as do the cattle and the standing crops. || 18 ||

When Jupiter is defeated by Mars, the Middle Country <note>original: "Madhya Desha," the central heartland of ancient India</note>, its sovereign rulers, and the cattle suffer.

# The Great Compilation
## Chapter 17

When Jupiter is defeated by **Saturn**, the people of Arjunayana, Vasati, Yaudheya, and Sibi, as well as the priestly class <note>original: "vipra"</note>, suffer.
<column-break/>
When Jupiter is defeated by **Mercury** <note>literally "the son of the Moon"</note>, the barbarians <note>original: "mleccha"</note>, those who are truthful, and those who live by the sword are destroyed; the Middle Country <term>Madhyadesha: the central region of ancient India, considered the cultural heartland</term> also faces ruin, along with whatever specific regions are assigned to Jupiter's influence.

When **Jupiter** is defeated by **Venus**, the foremost among those preparing for a military expedition <note>original: "yayi"</note> meets destruction. There arises a conflict between the priestly and warrior classes <note>original: "brahma-kshatra"</note>, and Indra <note>the god of rain</note> does not release the waters from the sky.

The regions of Kosala, Kalinga, Vanga <note>modern Bengal</note>, Vatsa, and Matsya, along with the Middle Country, suffer great distress, as do the eunuchs and the people of Shurasena.

When **Venus** is defeated by **Mars** <note>literally "the son of the Earth"</note>, there is the slaughter of military commanders and wars between kings. When Venus is defeated by **Mercury**, the mountain tribes are afflicted, milk production fails, and there is little rain.

When **Venus** is defeated by **Saturn** <note>literally "the son of the Sun"</note>, the leaders of guilds <note>original: "gana-mukhya"</note>, those who live by the sword, and the warrior class are oppressed, as are those things produced in water. Other effects follow the general rules of planetary influence.

->**The Effects of the Year of Jupiter**<-

During the auspicious year of the Preceptor of the Gods <note>Jupiter/Brihaspati</note>, the earth is satisfied on all sides by water from clouds that are elevated and streaked with various lightning bolts. The land abounds in crops and is endowed with the highest prosperity. || 15 ||

# The Great Compilation [Chapter 20]

The rays of the sun and moon are obscured, choked by excessive dust in the atmosphere; the reservoirs are depleted of water, and even the great rivers run thin. **(20)**

In some places, the crops perish due to a total lack of water; in others, they thrive where they have been sprinkled by moisture. When the year belongs to the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>, the Enemy of Vritra <note>Indra, the god of rain</note> pours down rain only sparingly. **(21)**

When the planets possess small or dim rays, occupy low positions in the sky, or are defeated by other planets in conjunction, they do not grant their full rewards. If they are the opposite, they provide nourishment and prosperity. Any misfortune predicted for an inauspicious year is intensified by an inauspicious month; likewise, good results are increased by good months. If the year and month are of opposing natures, the results are neutralized. **(22)**

## Chapter 21

->What science could possibly be superior to this? By knowing this alone, even in this destructive age of Kali <note>The Kali Yuga, or the present age of spiritual decline in Hindu cosmology</note>, a person becomes a seer of the three divisions of time—past, present, and future. (4)<-

Some authorities claim that the "days of conception" <note>The term 'Garbha' or conception refers to the formation of rain-clouds months before they actually fall</note> for clouds begin after the end of the bright half of the month of Karttika <note>October-November</note>. However, that is not the consensus. I shall now state the opinion of Garga and other ancient sages. (5)

From the first day of the bright half of the month of Margashirsha <note>November-December</note>, when the Moon enters the lunar mansion <term>Nakshatra: a sector of the sky marked by specific stars</term> of Purva-Ashadha, the symptoms of the "conception" of clouds are to be observed. (6)

On whatever day the Moon is positioned in a particular lunar mansion during the cloud's conception, the delivery <note>the actual rainfall</note> will occur exactly one hundred and ninety-five days later, according to the Moon's transit through that same mansion. (7)

Clouds conceived during the bright fortnight will be delivered in the dark fortnight; those conceived in the dark fortnight will fall in the bright. Those conceived by day will fall at night, and those conceived at night will fall by day. Those conceived during the twilight hours will likewise result in rain during the twilight. (8)

Conceptions that begin in the month of Margashirsha or the bright half of Pausha <note>December-January</note> generally yield only a small amount of fruit <note>minimal rainfall</note>.

# The Great Compilation
## Chapter 21

The sky is filled with clouds that are **broad, thick, smooth, and dense**, accompanied by clouds shaped like needles or razors, or appearing reddish in hue. The sky itself takes on the dark, glossy color of a crow's egg, yet the moon and stars remain clearly visible and pure. 15

Auspicious signs include the appearance of rainbows, deep rumbling thunder, lightning, and mock suns <note>parhelia or "sun dogs"</note> during a pleasant twilight. Birds and herds of wild animals should be heard making peaceful, gentle sounds in the directions presided over by the Moon, Shiva, or Indra <note>the North, Northeast, and East</note>. 16

The planets should appear large, moving in their proper clockwise orbits, with soft, glossy rays and free from any portents of calamity. The trees should have healthy, undamaged sprouts, and both humans and four-legged animals should appear joyful. 17

While all these signs generally nourish the "embryos" of the clouds, I shall now describe the specific characteristics produced by the nature of each season that lead to the growth of rain-clouds. 18

During the months of *Margashirsha* <note>November-December</note> and *Pausha* <note>December-January</note>, a red glow at twilight and clouds surrounded by halos are favorable. In *Margashirsha*, the cold should not be excessive, but in *Pausha*, there should be heavy falls of snow. 19

In the month of *Magha* <note>January-February</note>, there should be strong winds, and the sun and moon should appear dimmed or obscured by frost and mist.

When the weather is extremely cold and the sun is covered by clouds, its rising and setting are considered auspicious indicators for future rain. || 20 ||

In the month of **Phalguna** <note>mid-February to mid-March</note>, a dry and fierce wind, glossy clouds, incomplete halos around the sun or moon, and a sun that appears reddish-brown or copper-colored are beneficial signs. || 21 ||

In the month of **Chaitra** <note>mid-March to mid-April</note>, cloud embryos accompanied by wind, rain, and halos are auspicious. In the month of **Vaishakha** <note>mid-April to mid-May</note>, cloud embryos are beneficial when accompanied by dense clouds, wind, rain, lightning, and thunder. || 22 ||

Clouds that resemble the color of pearls or silver, or those that possess the dark hue of *Tamala* leaves <note>Garcinia xanthochymus</note>, blue lotuses, or colognes, and take the shapes of aquatic animals, contain abundant water within their embryos. || 23 ||

Clouds that have been heated by the intense rays of the sun and are moved by gentle breezes will, at the time of their "delivery" <note>the rainy season</note>, release water in torrents as if they were provoked to anger. || 24 ||

The following are signs of injury to the cloud embryos: meteors, thunderbolts, dust storms, "burning" of the horizon <note>unusual atmospheric redness</note>, earthquakes, "cities in the sky" <note>fata morgana or complex mirages</note>, pillar-shaped clouds, comets, planetary conflicts, and sudden thunderclaps in a clear sky. || 25 ||

# The Great Compilation
## Chapter 23: On the Quantity of Rainfall

Based on the first appearance of the moon or specific atmospheric portents, the quantity of water must first be declared. <note>The text refers to the "Pravarshana" or the first rainfall of the season as a diagnostic tool for the coming months.</note> ॥ 3 ॥

Some authorities claim that the rain will fall over an area of eighty miles <note>original: "dasha-yojana," where a yojana is roughly 8 miles</note> around the place where the portent is seen. However, according to the schools of **Garga, Vasishtha, and Parashara**, the extent is actually ninety-six miles. ॥ 4 ॥

Rain will generally fall most abundantly in those lunar mansions <term>Nakshatras: the 27 divisions of the sky through which the moon passes</term> where the portents were first observed. If the portents are seen in "destructive" mansions <note>referring to inauspicious astrological configurations</note> and not in others, then a total drought <term>Anavrishti</term> is to be expected. ॥ 5 ॥

The quantity of rain is measured in <term>Dronas: a traditional unit of liquid measure, roughly equivalent to 200 ounces or 1.6 gallons</term> according to the mansion the moon occupies:

| Lunar Mansion (Nakshatra) | Quantity of Rain |
| :--- | :--- |
| Hasta, Purvashadha, Mrigashirsha, Chitra, Revati, and Dhanishtha | 16 Dronas |
| Shatabhishak, Jyeshtha, and Swati | 4 Dronas |
| Krittika | 10 Dronas |
| Shravana, Magha, Anuradha, Bharani, and Mula | 14 Dronas |
| Purva Phalguni | 25 Dronas |
| Punarvasu | 20 Dronas |
| Vishakha and Uttarashadha | 20 Dronas |
| Ashlesha | 13 Dronas |
| Uttara Bhadrapada, Uttara Phalguni, and Rohini | 25 Dronas |

॥ 6–8 ॥

Having observed the positions correctly, I shall now set forth the meanings of the conjunction of the Moon with the asterism of Prajapati <note>The asterism Rohini, presided over by the creator deity Prajapati</note> in a concise manner, being prepared to explain them clearly. || 3 ||

## [Chapter 24]

The falling of meteors, lightning, and thunderbolts;
The burning of the horizons <note>a reddish atmospheric glow</note>, celestial crashes, and earthquakes;
The cries of wild beasts and birds—
All these should be observed and interpreted just as one interprets the clouds. || 25 ||

One should set out water-pots <term>Kumbhas: ritual earthen jars used for divination</term> marked with the names of the months, starting with Shravana <note>the first month of the rainy season, July-August</note>, arranged in a clockwise direction.
The month whose corresponding pot remains full will grant abundant rain;
If the pot is empty, a total lack of rain is to be predicted for that period. || 26 ||

Other pots may be marked with the names of kings,
And still others with the names of various regions.
By observing if they are broken, leaking, half-empty, or overflowing,
The fortunes of those kings and lands should be declared accordingly. || 27 ||

Whether the Moon is far or near,
Or situated anywhere along the Southern Path <note>the southern celestial latitude</note>;
If it joins with the star Rohini under these conditions,
One must predict nothing but hardship for the world. || 28 ||

When the Moon <note>original: "Shashanka," meaning 'the one marked with a hare'</note> touches Rohini and then passes to the north,
There will be good rains, yet many calamities will follow.
If the Moon moves to the north without touching the star,
It brings vast rainfall and general well-being. || 29 ||

When the Moon stands in the middle of the "Wagon of Rohini" <note>a specific V-shaped configuration of stars in the Taurus constellation</note>,
The people are left without any refuge or protection.

Whatever results were predicted for the conjunction of Rohini, all of those should also be considered for the Moon's conjunction with the stars Swati <note>Arcturus</note> and Ashadha <note>the Archer's stars</note> during the bright half of the month of Ashadha <note>June–July</note>. If it rains during the first part of the night when the Moon is in Swati, all crops will reach full growth. If it rains in the second part, sesame, mung beans, and black gram will thrive. If it rains in the third part, the summer crops will exist, but not the autumn ones. || 2 ||

If it rains in the first part of the day, there will be good rainfall throughout the season; if in the second part, the rain will be accompanied by insects and snakes. If rain is seen in the middle or latter part of the day, it will be moderate; but if it rains day and night, there will be continuous, uninterrupted rainfall. || 3 ||

# Brihat Samhita
### Chapter 26

"You are the daughter of Brahma, and you are celebrated as the Sun's radiance; by lineage, you belong to the family of Kashyapa, and by name, you are known as the Balance." <note>This is a formal invocation or mantra addressed to the ritual scale, personifying it as a deity to ensure the accuracy of the divination.</note> || 5 ||

->The scale should be made of linen cloth, bound with four threads;<-
->the slings for the pans should be six fingers-breadth in length.<-
->The length of the main strings should be ten fingers-breadth,<-
->and the distance between the two slings at the central beam should be exactly six fingers.<- || 6 ||

In the southern scale-pan, one should place gold; in the northern pan, the other substances and water should be placed. By observing the weight against water taken from wells, from flowing streams, or from natural lakes, one can predict whether the rainfall will be low, middling, or excellent. <note>The "other substances" refer to samples representing different sectors of society or the environment, as detailed in the next verse.</note> || 7 ||

Elephants are represented by their tusks; cattle, horses, and other animals by their hair; kings by gold; and the twice-born <term>dvija; the priestly and scholarly classes</term> by beeswax. Similarly, regions, years, months, and directions are represented by their respective symbolic substances. || 8 ||

A scale made of gold is the best; one of silver is middling; if these are unavailable, it should be made from Khadira wood <note>Acacia catechu</note>, or from the shaft of an arrow that has struck a man. The length of the balance beam should be one span <term>vitasti; approximately 9 inches</term>. || 9 ||

If the weight of a substance decreases in the scale, it indicates destruction or loss for that category; if the weight increases, it indicates growth and prosperity; if the weight remains equal, the result will be stable. This secret of the "Balance-Casket" has been told; a man should perform this during the <term>Prajeshayoga; the conjunction of the Moon with the Rohini asterism</term>. || 10 ||

# The Great Compilation
## Chapter 27

->**On the Signs of the Winds**<-

If, at the time of the celestial conjunction, a wind from the East—churned by the crashing of waves against the shores of the Eastern Ocean and struck by the mane-like rays of the sun and moon—should blow from the sky, then one should know that the Earth will be covered by masses of dark clouds that do not remain in one place. The land will be enriched by the autumn harvest and its surface adorned with the lush crops of the spring season. (1)

When the South-Eastern wind <note>original: "Agneya," the direction governed by Agni, the fire god</note>, skilled at striking the peaks of the Malaya mountains, blows during this conjunction as the divine Sun <note>original: "Patanga," literally 'the bird' or 'the flyer'</note> sets, then the Earth—constantly inflamed and its surface embraced by peaks of fire—seems to vomit heaps of ash through the hot exhalations of its own body. (2)

When the South wind blows harshly during this conjunction, making the monkeys dance among the trees and the spreading canopies of palm leaves and creepers, then the clouds—though rising with full effort like elephants—act like stingy farmers <note>original: "Kinasha," a term for a person who is miserly or a poor cultivator</note> prodded by goads, releasing only meager droplets of water. (3)

If the South-Western wind blows incessantly at sunset, swirling the clusters of fine cardamom, Lavali, and cloves across the ocean, then the Earth appears like a drunken bride of a ghost—fickle and covered with a heavy layer of human bone fragments, the result of deaths from hunger and thirst. (4)

When a gale from the West, flickering with the majesty of a great lion's mane due to the rising dust, blows at the moment the sun's rays fall, then the Earth—though filled with crops—will see wars started by great kings, and in various places, the ground will be soaked with constant fat, flesh, and blood. (5)

If, at the time of the full moon of the month of Ashadha <note>late June/early July</note>, as the Lord of Rays <note>the Sun</note> reaches the time of setting, a North-Western wind blows with increased velocity—an enemy to the clouds and mimicking the sound of a serpent...

One should recognize the earth as if it were an army of good fortune, filled with abundant happiness; it is marked solely by the joyful sprouting of crops and the croaking of frogs released from their silence, delighted by the streams of water. Regarding the inquiry into rainfall: if, during the bright fortnight <note>The waxing phase of the moon</note>, the Moon occupies a watery sign <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note> and is positioned in the Ascendant or a Cardinal house <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses in a birth chart</note>, it brings much water if aspected by benefic planets. If the person asking the question touches a wet object, or water itself, or something named after water, or if they are standing near water or about to perform an action involving water; or if, at the time of the inquiry, the word "water" is heard, the astrologer should declare: "There will be rain shortly, without a doubt." || 2 ||

If cattle gaze upward toward the sun, then water will fall from the sky without delay. || 8 ||

If the domestic animals do not wish to leave the house, and if they shake their ears and hooves; and if the dogs behave in this same manner as the livestock, one should declare that "water is about to fall." || 9 ||

When dogs stay upon the roofs of houses, or if they gaze upward toward the sky with mouths wide open; or if lightning appears during the day in the North-Eastern quarter <note>original: "pinaki-digbhava" – the direction of the wielder of the Pinaka bow, Shiva</note>, then the earth will be covered with excessive water. || 10 ||

When the moon <note>original: "himadidhiti" – the cold-rayed one</note> resembles the color of the eyes of a parrot or a pigeon, or appears like the color of honey; and when a mock sun <note>original: "pratishashi" – literally a 'counter-moon' or parhelion/paraselene effect</note> shines in the sky, then water falls from the heavens before long. || 11 ||

If there is thunder at night and lightning during the day, appearing red like blood and standing straight like a staff <term>Danda: a rod or staff, here referring to a vertical lightning bolt or atmospheric phenomenon</term>; and if a cool breeze blows from the East, then the arrival of water is imminent. || 12 ||

If the young sprouts of creepers point upward toward the sky; if birds bathe themselves in water or dust; and if reptiles perch upon the tips of grass blades, then the fall of water is very near. || 13 ||

# Brihat Samhita
## Chapter 28: Signs of Immediate Rain

->Page 145<-

When the evening clouds bear the colors of the peacock, the parrot, the blue jay, or the cuckoo; when they possess the luster of the China rose <note>original: "japā-kusuma"</note> or the red lotus; and when they take the shapes of water-waves, mountains, crocodiles, tortoises, boars, or fish, and are piled in many layers—then they will yield abundant water before long. || 14 ||

Those clouds which are white as lime or the moon at their edges, but possess the dark brilliance of collyrium <note>a traditional eye-salve</note> or a swarm of bees in their center; which are glossy, multi-layered, and shedding tiny droplets of water; which resemble a flight of stairs; and which move from the East to the West, or from the West to the East—these clouds will soon discharge a great quantity of water upon the earth. || 15 ||

If rainbows, cross-bars of light <note>term: "parigha" - an atmospheric phenomenon where a line of light crosses the sun</note>, mock suns, red vertical streaks, lightning, or halos are seen at the time of the sun's rising or setting, one should predict that plenty of water will fall very soon. || 16 ||

<insert>
If the sky resembles the color of a partridge's wing, and the flocks of birds chirp joyfully at the rising or setting of the sun, the clouds will release water day and night without delay. || 17 ||
</insert>

If the rays of the thousand-rayed sun <note>the Sun</note> appear unfailing and shoot upwards like the peaks of the sunset mountain, and if the clouds rumble with a sound that seems to vibrate along the very ground, that is a sign of a great downpour. || 18 ||

During the rainy season, if the Moon <note>original: "śītakara" - the cool-rayed one</note> is situated in the seventh house from Venus and is aspected by a benefic planet...

# The Great Compilation [Chapter 28]

If the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is situated in the ninth, fifth, or seventh house from the Sun, it leads to the arrival of water <note>rainfall</note>. || 19 ||

Generally, at the time of the rising or setting of the planets, during their conjunctions, when they transition between celestial circles <note>mandala-sankrame</note>, at the end of a fortnight <note>the new or full moon</note>, or at the end of the Sun's solstice, rain occurs; it is also certain to rain when the Sun enters the lunar mansion of Ardra. || 20 ||

Water falls during the conjunction of Mercury and Venus, Mercury and Jupiter, or Jupiter and Venus. However, the conjunction of Saturn and Mars brings danger from wind and fire, and no rain falls unless they are joined by other planets. || 21 ||

When the planets follow closely behind or move ahead of the Sun, they make the earth appear as if it were a single vast ocean <note>indicating torrential rain</note>. || 22 ||

->Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, titled "Signs of Immediate Rain," in the *Great Compilation* composed by the illustrious Varahamihira.<-

One should determine the easy availability of commodities and the successful production of crops by observing the abundance of fruits and flowers on the forest trees. || 1 ||

The *Kalama* rice <note>a fine variety of white rice</note> thrives when the *Shala* tree <note>Shorea robusta</note> is flourishing; the red rice thrives when the Red *Ashoka* tree is in full bloom.

# The Great Compilation ## [Chapter 29]

Gold is indicated by the flowers of the *Champaka* <note>Magnolia champaca; a fragrant yellow-orange flower</note>; and a wealth of coral is foretold by the *Bandhujiva* <note>Pentapetes phoenicea; a bright red flower</note>. Diamonds are represented by flowers resembling the *Kuruvaka* <note>Red amaranth or a variety of Barleria</note>, and cat's-eye gems <term>Vaidurya: a precious chrysoberyl gemstone</term> by the *Nandikavarta* <note>Pinwheel flower or Crape Jasmine</note>. || 8 ||

From the *Sinduvara* <note>Vitex negundo; a small tree with pale blue flowers</note> comes news of the Vindhya region; pearls are indicated by the *Kunkuma* <note>Saffron</note>; and safflower <note>Carthamus tinctorius</note> signifies the same. The King is represented by the red lotus, and the Minister is said to be represented by the blue lotus. || 9 ||

The Guild-leader <term>Shresthi: a prominent merchant or head of a trade guild</term> is indicated by "golden flowers" <note>likely the Cassia fistula or Laburnum</note>; Brahmins by the pink lotus; and Priests by the white water-lily. The Commander of the Army is represented by the *Saugandhika* <note>a highly fragrant variety of water-lily</note>, and an increase in gold is foretold by the *Arka* <note>Calotropis gigantea; the crown flower</note>. || 10 ||

Safety and prosperity are indicated by mangoes; fear by the *Bhallataka* <note>marking nut tree</note>; and health by the *Pilu* <note>Salvadora persica; the toothbrush tree</note>. Famine is foretold by the *Khadira* <note>Cutch tree</note> and *Shami* <note>Prosopis cineraria</note> trees, while a beautiful rainfall is indicated by the *Arjuna* trees. || 11 ||

Plenty of food <term>Subhiksha: a time of abundant crops and easy subsistence</term> is indicated by the flowers of the *Pichumanda* <note>Neem tree</note> and the *Naga* <note>Ironwood tree</note>; while wind is foretold by the *Kapittha* <note>Wood-apple</note>. A fear of drought is indicated by the *Nichula* <note>a variety of cane or Hijjal</note>, and a fear of disease arises from the *Kutaja* <note>Conessi tree</note>. || 12 ||

Sugarcane is indicated by the flowers of *Durva* and *Kusha* grasses; and fire is foretold by the *Kovidara* <note>Bauhinia or Orchid tree</note>.

# Chapter 30: Signs of Twilight

From the time the sun is half-set or half-risen until the stars in the sky become indistinct, that duration is known as the period of twilight <term>Sandhyakala: the transitional periods of dawn and dusk</term>. The following signs observed during this time yield specific results: || 1 ||

These signs include the behavior of deer and birds, the wind, halos <note>luminous circles around the sun or moon</note>, circles of light, "bolts" <note>atmospheric lines or bars across the sun</note>, clouds, "cloud-trees" <note>vertical cloud formations</note>, and rainbows; as well as "cities of the Gandharvas" <term>Fata Morgana: complex mirages appearing on the horizon</term>, sunbeams, rods of light, dust, oiliness, and various colors. || 2 ||

If a deer cries out loudly and fiercely many times, it foretells the destruction of the village. If the deer is facing the sun and crying loudly from the south, it brings about the destruction of the army. || 3 ||

->If the wind or birds move from right to left, there will be war;<-

->Or if the wind is mixed at twilight, it brings rain. || 4 ||<-

->During the morning twilight foretells the destruction of the country.<-
->If they cry out from the southern direction with their faces toward the sun,<-
->It signifies the capture of the city. || 5 ||<-

->When the wind is powerful enough to shake house-trees and gateways,<-
->Or when it raises clouds of dust and clods of earth;<-
->When the sound is terrifying and harsh,<-
->And birds fall from the sky—such a twilight is inauspicious. || 6 ||<-

->When the trees move their leaves only slightly, stirred by a gentle breeze,<-
->Or when the air is perfectly still;<-
->When the birds and wild beasts cry out with sweet and calm notes,<-
->Such a twilight is considered blessed. || 7 ||<-

->If at the time of twilight the sky is glossy,<-
->And marked by "Staffs" <note>Vertical light phenomena</note>, lightning, "Fish" <note>Mock suns or specific cloud shapes</note>, halos, or circles of light;<-
->And if the Bow of the Lord of Gods <note>The rainbow</note>, the "Line of Indra's Elephant" <note>A specific cloud formation</note>,<-
->And sunbeams are visible, they quickly bring rain. || 8 ||<-

->If these signs are broken, uneven, destroyed,<-
->Noisy, crooked, or turning from right to left...<-
